title: MHRA 2030 Strategy to modernise patient-centred regulation for the era of AI and personalised medicines
key_facts: The UK medicines regulator MHRA published its 2030 Strategy on 14 Oct 2026.
It covers all four nations of the UK.
Aims: more patient-centred regulation, faster access to safe and effective treatments, more data connectivity and global influence.
Mission stated as 'health and prosperity for all, through scientific excellence'.
Strategy says AI is transforming both regulated products and how organisations are run, and challenges traditional regulatory models.
Includes a Women's Health Plan, more diversity in clinical studies and a push against illegal medicines.
Industry and HRA statements welcome it; the page lists a section on transforming regulation with AI and MedTech methods.
quote_evidence: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has set out ambitious plans to translate cutting-edge scientific and technological innovation into better health outcomes for patients across all four nations of the UK, in its 2030 Strategy published today.
AI is transforming both regulated products and how organisations are run.

The MHRA’s new strategy is clear on speed, clear on standards and clear on how performance will be measured, with firm service guarantees, closer working with NICE and patients at the centre of every decision.
why_it_matters_hint: The regulator that approves medicines and medical devices in the UK is planning around AI, which shapes how fast such products reach patients.
notes: Official government page; the quoted praise comes from industry and the HRA, not independent assessment. The page text we got gives few AI specifics.
